---
title: "NRT and delayed mode"
format:
  html:
    page-layout: full
execute:
  echo: false
---

A flag set in delayed mode is likely to be an operator's decision rather
than an automated test's, so comparing it with nrtqclib asks a different
question from comparing two sets of NRT flags. The rest of the site already
keeps profiles with a delayed mode observation apart, by the data mode the
files declare. This page adds a group the files do not declare: **profiles
marked NRT whose flags look like delayed mode ones.**

The sign is the share of a profile's observations that the input flags and
nrtqclib does not. An automated test rarely rejects most of a profile; an
operator who judges a cast bad often rejects all of it. Delayed mode
profiles show it, and so do some profiles marked real time.

```{ojs}
//| output: false
app = import(new URL("assets/js/app.js", document.baseURI).href)
meta = app.loadAnalyses()
name = (id) => app.datasetName(meta, id)
table = app.analysisTable
byDataset = (a, b) => app.datasetOrder(meta, a.dataset_id) - app.datasetOrder(meta, b.dataset_id)
rule = meta ? meta.rules.estimated_delayed : null
groupLabel = (key) => meta.groups.find((g) => g.key === key)?.label ?? key
modeLabel = (key) => meta.data_modes.find((m) => m.key === key)?.label ?? key
percent = (value) => `${Math.round(100 * value)}%`
```

```{ojs}
meta === null ? app.analysesMissing() : html``
```

```{ojs}
meta ? md`**The rule.** A profile marked NRT${rule.groups.includes("unknown") ? ", or with no data mode," : ""} is estimated to be delayed mode when at least ${percent(rule.min_share)} of its observations with a usable input flag are flagged by the input and not by nrtqclib, in either variable. A variable counts only with at least ${rule.min_observations} such observations, so a profile of two flagged values out of two is not called. The threshold is a setting of the analysis; the table further down shows how the count moves with it.` : html``
```

## The groups

Every profile is filed under exactly one group, decided in this order: on
land (see [Depth](analyses-depth.qmd)), containing delayed mode, estimated
delayed mode, data mode unknown, and NRT. Only the last is compared item by
item on [Flag differences](analyses-flags.qmd).

```{ojs}
groupsTable = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("dm_groups") : null
groupRows = groupsTable
  ? app.widen(groupsTable, { index: ["dataset_id"], column: "group", value: "n_profiles" }).sort(byDataset)
  : []
meta ? table(groupRows, [
  { key: "dataset_id", label: "Product", align: "left", format: name },
  ...meta.groups.map((g) => ({ key: g.key, label: g.label, title: g.description }))
]) : html``
```

```{ojs}
meta ? app.analysisFigure(
  "dm_groups",
  "Each product's profiles by the group the analyses file them under.",
  "Stacked bars of the share of profiles in each group, per product."
) : html``
```

## The share flagged by the input alone

```{ojs}
meta ? app.analysisFigure(
  "dm_share",
  `Profiles by the share of their observations flagged by the input alone, coloured by the data mode their files declare. Profiles with no such observation, most of every product, are left out and counted in the table below. The dashed line is the threshold, ${percent(rule.min_share)}.`,
  "Histograms of the input-only share per product, split by declared data mode."
) : html``
```

The shares are two humps: profiles where the input flags a few values
nrtqclib does not, and profiles where it flags nearly all of them. The
trough between them is where the threshold belongs, and the count of
profiles at or above it barely moves across it.

```{ojs}
thresholds = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("dm_threshold") : null
hist = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("dm_share_hist") : null
thresholdRows = thresholds
  ? app.widen(thresholds, { index: ["dataset_id", "data_mode", "n_eligible"], column: "threshold", value: "n_profiles", name: (t) => `t${t}` })
      .map((row) => ({
        ...row,
        zero: (hist ?? []).filter((h) => h.dataset_id === row.dataset_id && h.data_mode === row.data_mode && h.bin_hi === 0)
          .reduce((s, h) => s + h.n_profiles, 0)
      }))
      .sort((a, b) => byDataset(a, b) || a.data_mode.localeCompare(b.data_mode))
  : []
thresholdKeys = thresholds ? [...new Set(thresholds.map((t) => t.threshold))].sort((a, b) => a - b) : []
meta ? table(thresholdRows, [
  { key: "dataset_id", label: "Product", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "data_mode", label: "Declared", align: "left", format: modeLabel },
  { key: "n_eligible", label: "With a share", title: `Profiles with at least ${rule.min_observations} observations with a usable input flag in a variable` },
  { key: "zero", label: "Share 0" },
  ...thresholdKeys.map((t) => ({ key: `t${t}`, label: `At or above ${percent(t)}` }))
]) : html``
```

```{ojs}
meta ? app.analysisFigure(
  "dm_threshold",
  "Profiles at or above each threshold. Dashed: profiles marked NRT or with no data mode, the ones the rule files as estimated delayed mode. Solid: profiles already in delayed mode that the same rule would catch, which says how much of delayed mode the rule can see at all.",
  "Line charts of profile counts against the threshold, per region."
) : html``
```

## What leaving them out changes

The flag agreement of each group, per 1,000 of its observations. The
estimated group is chosen for its input-only flags, so its "original only"
rates are high by construction. The row to read is NRT: what its rates
would have been with the estimated profiles in it is the two rows
combined, and the estimated ones hold most of the input-only flags of the
profiles marked NRT. The delayed mode group is not a yardstick for the
estimate: most declared delayed mode profiles have no input-only flag at
all, as the histogram shows.

```{ojs}
rateRows = groupsTable
  ? groupsTable
      .filter((r) => r.group !== "land")
      .map((r) => {
        const row = { dataset_id: r.dataset_id, group: r.group, n_profiles: r.n_profiles, n_obs: r.n_obs };
        for (const v of meta.variables) {
          for (const s of ["original_only", "nrtqclib_only", "agree_bad"]) {
            row[`${v.name}_${s}`] = app.perThousandOf(r[`${v.name}_n_${s}`], r.n_obs);
          }
        }
        return row;
      })
  : []
groupRates = [...rateRows].sort((a, b) => byDataset(a, b) || meta.groups.findIndex((g) => g.key === a.group) - meta.groups.findIndex((g) => g.key === b.group))
meta ? table(groupRates, [
  { key: "dataset_id", label: "Product", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "group", label: "Group", align: "left", format: groupLabel },
  { key: "n_profiles", label: "Profiles" },
  ...meta.variables.flatMap((v) => [
    { key: `${v.name}_original_only`, label: `${v.label}: original only`, format: app.formatRate },
    { key: `${v.name}_nrtqclib_only`, label: `nrtqclib only`, format: app.formatRate },
    { key: `${v.name}_agree_bad`, label: `both`, format: app.formatRate }
  ])
]) : html``
```

## Where they come from

If the estimate picks up reprocessing rather than chance, its profiles
should gather on a few platforms instead of spreading thinly. For each
platform with any: how many of its profiles could be estimated (marked NRT
or with no data mode), how many were, and how many it has in declared
delayed mode.

```{ojs}
platforms = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("dm_estimated_platforms") : null
meta ? table((platforms ?? []).sort((a, b) => b.n_estimated - a.n_estimated), [
  { key: "dataset_id", label: "Product", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "platform_code", label: "Platform", align: "left", format: (v) => v },
  { key: "n_profiles", label: "Profiles at sea" },
  { key: "n_candidates", label: "NRT or unknown" },
  { key: "n_estimated", label: "Estimated" },
  { key: "share", label: "Share", format: (_, r) => app.formatShare(r.n_estimated, r.n_candidates) },
  { key: "n_delayed", label: "Declared delayed" }
]) : html``
```

Every estimated profile is listed in
[the table this page reads](data/analyses/tables/dm_estimated_profiles.csv).
